motion.tooltip.advanced_settings_1eb415: Open the optional seed setting for HY-Motion.
motion.tooltip.choose_a_soma_bvh_file_80: Select a BVH motion clip. MotionBricks uses its poses to create a transition; it does not rig or retarget a character.
motion.tooltip.describe_the_motion_6cbae: Describe the action, pace, and style you want HY-Motion to generate. It creates a 30 fps skeletal BVH clip; it does not rig or retarget a character.
motion.tooltip.duration_in_seconds_388a7: Set the HY-Motion clip length from 1 to 12 seconds. Longer clips take more time and memory.
motion.tooltip.guidance_74122b: Set how closely HY-Motion follows your description, from 0 to 20. Higher guidance can constrain the motion more strongly.
motion.tooltip.maximum_length_tokens_b7d: Set the longest generated transition length. One token represents four frames; choose a value from 6 to 16 and no less than the minimum.
motion.tooltip.minimum_length_tokens_e9d: Set the shortest generated transition length. One token represents four frames; choose a value from 6 to 16.
motion.tooltip.motion_model_c65fac: Choose how to create motion: HY-Motion makes a human BVH clip from text; MotionBricks makes a transition from poses in a SOMA BVH file.
motion.tooltip.remove_pose_file_d98441: Clear the selected BVH file so you can choose another one.
motion.tooltip.sampling_steps_40d9b3: Set how many refinement steps HY-Motion uses, from 1 to 100. More steps can take longer.
motion.tooltip.seed_d07208: Use the same number with the same prompt and settings to help reproduce an HY-Motion result. Leave blank to use the default seed.
motion.tooltip.soma_motion_clip_931fd9: Choose the source BVH motion file for MotionBricks. It must use a Y-up SOMA skeleton in centimeters, be 30, 60, or 120 fps, and be no larger than 10 MiB.
motion.tooltip.starting_window_920171: Choose the zero-based frame where MotionBricks reads the starting pose window. Frame numbers use a 30 fps timebase, and the window needs four frames.
motion.tooltip.target_poses_to_use_fc684: Choose how many of the four target-window poses MotionBricks reads, from 1 to 4. The first pose sets the destination; more poses add velocity and acceleration.
motion.tooltip.target_window_daba34: Choose the zero-based frame where MotionBricks reads the target pose window. Frame numbers use a 30 fps timebase, and the window needs four frames.
motion.tooltip.variations_7be51e: Queue 1 to 4 HY-Motion clips as separate jobs. Each uses the next seed after the seed above, or its own random seed when the seed is blank.
